_meta.indication: Adjunctive treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD) and treatment of schizophrenia

pivotal_trials.design: Multinational, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, fixed-dose trial of brexpiprazole 1, 2, and 4 mg/day vs placebo
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to Week 6 in PANSS Total Score (MMRM)
pivotal_trials.n: Analyzed per arm: Brex 1 mg N=117, 2 mg N=179, 4 mg N=181, placebo N=180
pivotal_trials.result: Brexpiprazole 4 mg/day statistically superior to placebo in PANSS change at Week 6 (LS mean difference -6.5, p=0.0022); 1 mg (-3.4, p=0.16) and 2 mg (-3.1, p=0.15) not significant

pivotal_trials.design: Fixed-dose, multinational, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of brexpiprazole 0.25, 2, and 4 mg/day vs placebo
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to Week 6 in PANSS Total Score
pivotal_trials.n: Analyzed per arm: Brex 0.25 mg N=87, 2 mg N=180, 4 mg N=178, placebo N=178
pivotal_trials.result: Both brexpiprazole 2 mg/day (LS mean difference -8.72, p<0.0001) and 4 mg/day (-7.64, p=0.0006) statistically superior to placebo in PANSS change at Week 6; CGI-S also improved for both doses (4 mg/day -0.38, p=0.0012; 2 mg/day -0.33, p=0.0056)

nct_ctgov.title: Study of the Effectiveness of Three Different Doses of OPC-34712 in the Treatment of Adults With Acute Schizophrenia

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3 fixed-dose study of brexpiprazole 2 mg/day + ADT vs placebo + ADT, single dose compared to add-on placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Depressed patients with inadequate response to prospective treatment with antidepressant (ADT) alone
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline (end of Phase A) to Week 14 in MADRS Total Score for brexpiprazole 2 mg + ADT vs placebo + ADT
pivotal_trials.n: Per arm: Brex 2 mg + ADT N=187, placebo + ADT N=191
pivotal_trials.result: Brexpiprazole 2 mg + ADT superior to placebo + ADT in MADRS change at Week 14 (LS mean difference -3.12; 95% CI -4.70, -1.54; p=0.0001)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions were weight increased and akathisia in MDD (>=5% and at least twice placebo) and weight increased in schizophrenia (>=4% and at least twice placebo). Metabolic changes (cholesterol, triglycerides, body weight), prolactin increase, and orthostatic hypotension noted as class effects.
target_moa: Atypical antipsychotic; partial agonist at 5-HT1A and D2 neuroreceptors with additional activity at noradrenergic receptors

boxed_warning.content: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with antipsychotics (REXULTI not approved for this use); and increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors with antidepressants in patients aged 24 years and younger

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an advisory committee because trial designs were similar to previously approved products and the data did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues

description.text: Added treatment of agitation associated with Alzheimer's dementia as a new indication

citations.quote: With this submission, the Applicant's proposed indication is for the treatment of agitation associated with Alzheimer's dementia (AAD). This product is currently available as tablets for oral administration, including dosage strengths of 0.25 mg, 0.5 mg, 1 mg, 2 mg, 3 mg, and 4 mg. The proposed starting dosage regimen is 0.5 mg taken orally once daily on Days 1 to 7, followed by titration to 1 mg once daily on Days 8 through 14, and 2 mg on Day 15. The proposed recommend target dosage regimen is 2 mg once daily. After at least 14 days at 2 mg once daily, the dosage regimen can be increased to the maximum recommended daily dosage of 3 mg, based on clinical response and tolerability.

summary.text: Standard-review NME NDA for brexpiprazole (Rexulti) submitted July 11, 2014 with a July 11, 2015 PDUFA goal date; approved on direct clinical endpoints (PANSS for schizophrenia, MADRS for adjunctive MDD) without referral to an advisory committee, with pediatric PREA requirements and maintenance-study commitments.

Proposed In

The applicant is seeking approval for the treatment of schizophrenia and the adjunctive treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD). Sufficient evidence has been submitted to confirm efficacy for both indications; the safety profile of this NME has been evaluated and characterized adequately so that the drug may be used safely according to negotiated labeling.

Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated and received July 11, 2014, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for REXULTI (brexpiprazole) Tablets 0.25 mg, 0.5 mg, 1 mg, 2 mg, 3 mg, and 4 mg.

Your application for **REXULTI** (brepiprazole) was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the clinical trial designs are similar to previously approved products for the adjunctive treatment of major depressive disorder and schizophrenia.
